anchor: Presenter: Yasir Dhaifallah O Alyoubi Student ID: 24724078
replacement: Abstract. This report presents HALAH, a trust-oriented authorisation framework in which patient consent is represented as an evaluable consent object C = (I, A, P, T, L, E) rather than as a static permission record. The framework establishes trustworthy participants through decentralised identifiers and verifiable credentials, requires threshold-based approval by the guardian set G, enforces purpose, data-scope, temporal and jurisdictional constraints at every access request, and records auditable evidence of each decision. A prototype has been implemented and demonstrated on the Ethereum Sepolia test network, including consent activation, a granted request, a refused out-of-jurisdiction request, on-chain revocation and independent verification of the recorded transactions. The formal security analysis of the stated properties remains the subject of the next stage of the research.
